title: feat(formula,objectql): read one hop through a lookup in a validation predicate
body:
Fixes #18682

Clause-②: yes

A validation rule can now read one hop through a lookup. `record.account.type` on an opportunity resolves the owning account's field instead of faulting with `runtime: No such key: type` — and because a broken validation is fail-closed, that fault previously rejected **every** write on the object, so the rule could not be authored at all.

## The shape

The engine statically analyses each predicate, learns exactly which reference fields it reads through and which related fields it names, loads those rows **before** evaluation, and binds them in place of the id. There is no `os.lookup(...)` / `os.exists` / `os.count` — those stay removed, and `packages/formula/src/eval-context-no-query-api.test.ts` stays green untouched. Every registered function is still pure once `now` is pinned.

**No new evaluation-context mechanism was added.** The related rows arrive through the existing `record` root, hydrated by the engine exactly as it already hydrates a row for `$expand` readers and exactly as it already resolves `EvaluateRulesOptions.parent` and hands it over. `buildScope()` is untouched, so the CEL variable surface does not widen.

Two deliberate differences from the `parent` precedent:

- the rows are read under the **acting user**, through the engine's own `find` path, so the referenced object's CRUD gate, RLS and FLS all apply (`parent` reads as system, because a master-detail lock is a property of the header's state, not of the caller's visibility of it);
- an unresolved row is left **absent** on purpose. No id, row gone, refused by the security layer, read threw — all four leave the field unbound, the traversal faults, and the write is **rejected**. Never silently true, and never silently false.

Hydration is **per rule** and onto a **copy**. Per rule, because hydrating a field replaces its stored id with the related record and a sibling rule comparing the bare id must keep seeing the id. Onto a copy, because the record handed to a rule is the real write payload — hydrating it in place would send the expanded object to the driver in place of the foreign key.

## Two shapes refused at authoring time

Both fault at evaluation today, so neither removes anything that works — the refusal replaces a per-row runtime fault with one loud message naming the repair:

| Shape | Write instead |
| --- | --- |
| a reference field read both through the relationship and as a plain value | `record.account.id` for the value comparison |
| a read deeper than one hop | denormalise onto the related object, or read it in a hook |

Gated on `fieldTypes`, which is what tells a reference field from an object-valued one: `record.address.city` traverses today and keeps traversing.

## Scope

Object validation rules (`script` / `cross_field`) only — the seam that is fail-closed, and therefore the only one where an unreadable related field can produce the loud refusal the permission rule requires. The field-level `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / option `visibleWhen` predicates fail **open** and are deliberately out; RLS predicates are out; depth is one hop.

## Acceptance

`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json` gains `records-forms.predicate-relationship-traversal`, covering the three ruled outcomes, plus a dogfood case on the showcase app: `showcase_invoice` now refuses an invoice against a churned account **on the server**. Its `account` picker already scoped churned accounts out of the dropdown, which is exactly why the rule earns its place — a picker filter is a UI affordance, not a server guarantee, and REST, imports, flows and agents never touch the picker.

## Verification

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `@objectstack/formula` test | 34 files / 938 tests pass |
| `@objectstack/objectql` typecheck + test | clean; 304 files / 5072 tests pass |
| `@objectstack/example-showcase` test | 29 files / 384 tests pass |
| `@objectstack/lint` test (consumer) | 108 files / 4111 tests pass |
| `@objectstack/rest` test (consumer) | 194 files / 3265 pass, 1 skipped |
| `@objectstack/runtime` test (consumer) | 272 files / 3799 pass, 1 skipped |
| `@objectstack/plugin-security` test (consumer) | 117 files / 2249 tests pass |
| `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` test (consumer) | 37 files / 913 tests pass |
| derived gate families | 66 commands, 63 green first pass; see below |

**Reverse verification.** Hydration was ablated through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with the mutation proved on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob `77f25648d742` to `0a804a640bff`) and the restore proved byte-identical to `HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`. Predicted direction was red; observed red. Honest reading of the magnitude: **2 of 15** cases discriminate — the accept case and the case asserting the refusal carries the *authored* message. The bare `toThrow(ValidationError)` cases stay green under ablation because an unhydrated rule also throws, just for the wrong reason, which is why that second assertion exists.

**Lint, narrowed and declared.** `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 11 changed source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings, file count read from `--format json`. The narrowing is a measurement rather than a skip because `eslint.config.mjs` states and measures that this repo "never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file", so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide sweep remains CI's.

Two gate readings that are **NOT MEASURED** rather than green, stated as such:

- `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` exits 2 and refuses: this checkout is shallow and its oldest visible commit sits inside the 90-day window. The gate declines to print a ratio it cannot compute rather than emit a caveated one. CI clones deep.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first read `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` against a partially built tree, then a mid-build state; on a settled tree it passes (104 entry points, 620 CommonJS files).

One gate finding was real and is fixed in this PR: the new batched read went through `as any` and grew the query-options-erasure ratchet on `engine.ts` from 8 to 9. The options bag is declared, so it is now named (`EngineQueryOptions`); the ratchet's unswept count drops 68 to 67.

## Acceptance notes

- `PredicateRule.fields` is read by the runtime (`checkPredicate` derives the violation's field from `rule.fields?.[0]`) but the spec's `script` rule schema **refuses** the key — authoring one is an `unrecognized_keys` parse error, which is how the showcase rule first failed. So for authored rules that read is always `undefined` and the violation always attributes to `_record`. Noted, not filed and not fixed here: it is inert rather than harmful, and it is not this card's surface.
